title: Related rates and time differentiation
section: Related Rates ▷ Differentiating a geometric constraint
terms: related rates; instantaneous rate; time derivative; rate of change.

exposition.text:
Related-rates problems connect time-dependent quantities through a geometric or algebraic
constraint. Differentiate the constraint with respect to time before inserting the particular
2 2 2
instantaneous values. For example, x + y = L with fixed L gives x dx/dt + y dy/dt = 0. If a
supposedly fixed quantity actually varies, its derivative must also be included.
Track units and signs: a decreasing length has negative derivative, whereas its speed of decrease
is the positive magnitude. Similar triangles may provide a relation among hidden variables,
such as radius and height in a cone. Rates can become large near singular configurations, so a
numerical answer should also be checked against the geometry.

question.text:
Water fills a cone whose height is twice its radius at every water level. If the water volume
increases at 3π cubic units per minute, how fast does the water height rise when it is 3?
(A) 1/3 (B) 2/3 (C) 1 (D) 4/3 (E) 3

solution.text:
2 3 2
With r = h/2, V = πr h/3 = πh /12. Thus dV/dt = (πh /4)dh/dt. At h = 3, 3π =
(9π/4)dh/dt, so dh/dt = 4/3.

When the base is 5 units from the wall, what is the rate of change of the area of the triangle
enclosed by the ladder, wall, and floor?
(A) −119/12 (B) −5/6 (C) 5/6 (D) 119/12 (E) 12

solution.text:
2 2 ′ ′
At that instant the height is 12. From x + y = 169, y = −xx /y = −5/6. Since A = xy/2,

question.text:
A sphere’s volume grows at 12π units per second. At radius 2, how fast does its surface area
grow?
(A) 24π (B) 48π (C) 3π (D) 12π (E) 6π

solution.text:
′ 2 ′ ′ ′
Since V = 4πr r , the radial rate is 3/4. Then A = 8πrr = 8π · 2 · 3/4 = 12π.

question.text:
A searchlight is 30 meters from a straight wall. Its beam makes angle θ with the perpendicular
to the wall and rotates at dθ/dt = 1/10 radian per second. How fast does the spot move along
the wall when it is 40 meters from the nearest point on the wall?
(A) 3 m/s (B) 4 m/s (C) 5 m/s (D) 25/3 m/s (E) 40/3 m/s

solution.text:
2
If x is the spot distance, x = 30 tan θ, so dx/dt = 30 sec θ dθ/dt. At x = 40, tan θ = 4/3
2
and sec θ = 25/9. Thus the speed is 30(25/9)(1/10) = 25/3 meters per second. An angular
rate must be converted using radians and the geometric derivative.

question.text:
A gas obeys PV = kT with fixed k > 0. At an instant, pressure increases at 3% per second
and absolute temperature decreases at 1% per second. What is the instantaneous relative rate

(C) 2% per second (D) 3% per second
(E) 4% per second

solution.text:

treated as fixed.
